# Orqafy — Phase 7 Backend Feature Spec (PROPOSAL)
# PROPOSAL for owner redline — generated by architect; NOT yet merged into PRODUCT.md (Rule 1: humans edit PRODUCT.md).

> **What this is.** A concrete, redline-ready Phase 7 feature specification derived from the
> wiring-program gap catalog (`docs/WIRING_NEEDS_SPEC.md` per-wave W1–W12 + `docs/UI_BACKEND_GAPS.md`
> roll-up). Each cataloged gap is an *unsurfaced* backend procedure (the router/mutation exists and
> is tested; no UI authors the action). This file proposes **what to build, which entities/procedures,
> which UI surface, and acceptance criteria** for each, with framework-default implementation
> decisions already made. Genuine product-direction forks are flagged `⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION`.
>
> **Locked stack (applies to every entry).** Next.js (App Router) · tRPC · Prisma · Auth.js v5 ·
> PostgreSQL (separate-schema-per-tenant; `search_path` switched per request — Orqafy's tenancy
> exception, so NO `tenant_id` column on ERP entities; schema IS the boundary) · Valkey · BullMQ ·
> MinIO→S3 · shadcn/ui · Tailwind. **Security L1–L6 always on:** L3 RBAC via `rbac.ts` middleware,
> L5 AuditLog on every mutation, L6 Prisma guardrails. All forms = React Hook Form + Zod; all tables
> = TanStack; all confirms = shadcn `AlertDialog`.
>
> **Global default decisions (applied everywhere unless an entry overrides):**
> - **Form pattern:** create/edit = dedicated route (`.../new`, `.../[id]/edit`) when the form has a
>   line-item/multi-section editor or >6 fields; shadcn `Dialog` (modal) for ≤6-field single-entity
>   forms (contacts, tax rates, categories, fund sources). Rationale: routes are deep-linkable and
>   survive validation churn; modals keep light CRUD in-context.
> - **Lifecycle/authority actions** (approve, post, void, terminate, suspend): shadcn `AlertDialog`
>   confirm + role gate at the `rbac.ts` layer. Reason-capture textarea wherever the router requires
>   `reason`/`notes`.
> - **State sync:** optimistic update for non-destructive toggles; `invalidate`+refetch for
>   money-/inventory-/lifecycle-affecting actions (correctness over snappiness).
> - **Action bars:** one reusable `<StatusTransitionActionBar>` component (drives PO/payroll/project/
>   task/ticket/invoice state machines) — build once in Foundations, reuse across epics.

---

## Foundations (build first — unblock everything else)

### F1 — RSC→tRPC server-caller helper
- **Build:** a `createServerCaller()` helper (wrapping `createCallerFactory` with the request's
  auth session + tenant `search_path` context) so RSC pages and Server Actions invoke tRPC
  procedures instead of reading Prisma directly. Today `createCallerFactory` is used only in tests.
- **Entities/procedures:** none new — infra. Threads existing `context.ts` session + tenant resolution.
- **UI surface:** none. Internal.
- **Why first:** every "route this mutation through a router for L5 AuditLog + centralized RBAC"
  requirement (W12 platform-admin hardening, and any audit-on-mutation guarantee) is blocked on this.
- **Acceptance:** an RSC page can call a `protectedProcedure` and receive tenant-scoped data; a
  mutation invoked via the server-caller writes an AuditLog row; existing direct-Prisma reads still pass.

### F2 — Invoicing partial-payment model + mutation
- **Build:** an `invoice.recordPayment` mutation that records a partial or full payment against an
  invoice, updating `amountPaid` / `balance` and transitioning status to `partially_paid` or `paid`.
- **Entities:** `Invoice` (`amountPaid`, `balance`, status `partially_paid`/`paid` already in schema);
  add an `InvoicePayment` ledger row (id, invoiceId, amount, fundSourceId, method, paidAt, recordedBy)
  so each payment is auditable and links to the Banking fund-source ledger.
- **Procedures:** `invoice.recordPayment` (new); `invoice.markPaid` becomes a thin "pay full balance"
  convenience over it.
- **UI surface:** Banking/money-movement epic (see Epic 4).
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D1 (does recording an invoice payment auto-post a Banking
  income transaction to the linked fund source, or is it a separate manual step?).
- **Acceptance:** recording a payment < balance sets `partially_paid` and decrements `balance`;
  recording payment == balance sets `paid`; over-payment rejected; AuditLog written.

## Epic 1 — High-frequency CRUD (form-driven; shared create/edit + toggle pattern)

### 1.1 CRM — Customers, Contacts, Credit (W1, 8 procedures)
- **Build:** customer create/edit, customer activate/deactivate, contact add/edit/delete, credit-account
  config + enable/disable.
- **Entities:** `Customer`, `Contact`, customer credit fields.
- **Procedures:** `crm.customerCreate`, `crm.customerUpdate`, `crm.customerToggleActive`,
  `crm.contactCreate`, `crm.contactUpdate`, `crm.contactDelete`, `crm.creditUpsert`, `crm.creditToggleActive`.
- **UI surface:** `crm/customers/new` + `crm/customers/[id]/edit` (route — multi-section form: identity,
  tier, primary contact). On `crm/customers/[id]`: a Contacts panel (add/edit/delete via modal +
  `AlertDialog` on delete), a Credit panel (config modal: currency, limit, terms; enable/disable toggle),
  and a deactivate action in the detail action bar.
- **Defaults:** tier defaults `regular`; one primary contact enforced; deactivate = `AlertDialog` confirm,
  optimistic toggle.
- **Acceptance:** create/edit round-trips all fields; toggling active reflects optimistically and persists;
  contact CRUD updates the panel without full reload; credit config validates limit ≥ 0; every mutation
  audit-logged.

### 1.2 Inventory — Products, Categories, Warehouses, Movements (W4, 12 procedures)
- **Build:** product add/edit/toggle, category add/edit/toggle, warehouse add/edit/toggle, record movement,
  transfer stock, adjust stock.
- **Entities:** `Product`, `Category`, `Warehouse`, `StockMovement`.
- **Procedures:** `inventory.productCreate/productUpdate/productToggleActive`,
  `categoryCreate/categoryUpdate/categoryToggleActive`, `warehouseCreate/warehouseUpdate/warehouseToggleActive`,
  `stockMovementCreate`, `stockTransfer`, `stockAdjustment`.
- **UI surface:** Add/Edit Product = route (`inventory/products/new`, `.../[id]/edit`) — name, sku, unit,
  baseCost, category picker, active toggle. Category + Warehouse management = modal-driven panels on their
  respective list pages (≤6 fields each). "Record Movement" / "Transfer Stock" / "Adjust Stock" = modal forms
  surfacing the router's transactional validation; the ledger stays display-only.
- **Defaults:** Adjust Stock (inventory-affecting) = `AlertDialog` confirm + required reason; refetch ledger
  after any movement.
- **Acceptance:** product CRUD validates unique sku; transfer rejects insufficient-source-stock per router;
  adjustment requires reason and writes the offsetting movement; ledger refreshes post-action; all audited.

### 1.3 HR — Employees + DTR leave/attendance CRUD slice (W7, employee + leave-request subset)
- **Build (CRUD slice only):** employee add/edit, leave-request create. (Payroll-run + attendance-approval
  state machines move to Epic 2; terminate is an authority action also in Epic 2.)
- **Entities:** `Employee` (+ linked `User`, gov IDs, banking, emergency contact), `LeaveRequest`.
- **Procedures:** `employee.create`, `employee.update`, `dtr.leaveRequestCreate`.
- **UI surface:** `employees/new` + `employees/[id]/edit` (route — links a User, employmentType, dateHired,
  compensation, gov IDs SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG/TIN, banking, emergency contact). "Request Leave" modal on
  `dtr/page.tsx` (type, date range, reason).
- **Acceptance:** employee create links exactly one User; gov-ID fields validate format; leave request
  rejects end-before-start; audited.

## Epic 2 — Workflow / state-machine surfaces (shared `<StatusTransitionActionBar>`)

### 2.1 Purchasing — PO lifecycle + goods receipt + vendors (W5, 11 procedures)
- **Procedures:** `purchasing.vendor.create/update/deactivate`; `po.create/update`;
  `po.submit/approve/markOrdered/cancel`; `goodsReceipt.create`.
- **Entities:** `Vendor`, `PurchaseOrder`, `PurchaseOrderItem`, `PurchaseOrderItemAllocation`, `GoodsReceipt`,
  `GoodsReceiptItem`.
- **UI surface:** Add/Edit Vendor = modal (deactivate = confirm). "New PO" = route (`purchasing/orders/new`)
  with vendor picker + multi-row line-item editor + optional per-item stock/project_expense/company_expense
  **allocation** rows (router validates allocation sums == line qty + type-specific IDs). PO detail =
  `<StatusTransitionActionBar>` (draft → pending_approval → approved → ordered → cancelled; approve/cancel
  role-gated + confirm). "Receive Goods" = route/modal against an ordered PO (per-line quantityReceived /
  quantityRejected, notes) — inventory-affecting, confirm + refetch.
- **Acceptance:** PO builder blocks submit when allocation sums ≠ line qty; approve/cancel gated to authority
  role; goods receipt increments stock and prompts to process pending allocations; full state machine audited.

### 2.2 Accounting — Chart of accounts + journal + fiscal/tax (W6, 10 procedures)
- **Procedures:** `account.create/update/toggleActive`; `journalEntry.create/post/reverse`;
  `fiscalYear.create`; `taxRate.create`.
- **Entities:** `Account`, `JournalEntry`, `JournalLine`, `FiscalYear`, `TaxRate`.
- **UI surface:** Chart-of-accounts management page (account create/edit modal + toggle). Journal-entry
  builder = route (header date/ref + balanced multi-line debit/credit editor with account pickers; client
  validates debits == credits before submit). Post/reverse = `<StatusTransitionActionBar>` authority actions
  on the entry detail (confirm + reason on reverse). "New Fiscal Year" + "Add Tax Rate" = modals.
- **Acceptance:** journal builder rejects unbalanced entries; post is idempotent and locks the entry;
  reverse generates the offsetting entry; all audited.

### 2.3 HR — Payroll run lifecycle + termination + attendance approvals (W7 remainder)
- **Procedures:** `payroll.create/process/approve/markPaid`; `employee.terminate`;
  `dtr.attendanceApprove/attendanceReject`; `dtr.leaveRequestApprove/leaveRequestReject`.
- **Entities:** `PayrollRun`, `Payslip`, `Employee`, `Attendance`, `LeaveRequest`.
- **UI surface:** "New Payroll Run" form (period start/end, currency, employee-selection policy). Payroll-run
  detail = `<StatusTransitionActionBar>` (draft → processing → approved → paid; money-affecting authority
  actions, confirm + role gate). "Terminate" action on employee detail (confirm, sets dateTerminated).
  Attendance-review + leave-request surfaces gain approve/reject action controls.
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D2 (DTR time-clock device model — clock-in/clock-out UX).
- **Acceptance:** payroll cannot skip states; markPaid posts to ledger (per Banking integration) exactly
  once; terminate gated to HR authority; approvals audited.

### 2.4 Projects + Tasks (W8, 8 + 13 procedures)
- **Procedures (projects):** `project.create/update`, `project.complete/archive`,
  `project.expense.recordProjectExpense`, `project.milestone.create/update/complete`.
- **Procedures (tasks):** `tasks.taskCreate/taskUpdate/taskUpdateStatus/taskAssign/taskUnassign/
  taskAddStatusReport`; `tasks.todoCreate/todoUpdate/todoDelete/todoComplete/todoAddAttachment`.
- **Entities:** `Project`, `Milestone`, `ProjectExpense`, `Task`, `TaskAssignment`, `TaskStatusReport`,
  `TaskAttachment`, `ToDo`, `ToDoAttachment`.
- **UI surface:** New/Edit Project = route (`projects/new`, `projects/[id]/edit` — name, customer picker,
  manager, status, dates, budget). complete/archive = action-bar authority actions. "Record Expense" modal on
  the project expenses surface. Milestone management on the milestones tab. New/Edit Task = route or modal;
  **task detail route** introduced (cards currently link nowhere) carrying assignee picker, status report,
  and a per-task ToDo checklist. `taskUpdateStatus` = kanban drag-and-drop **or** per-card status dropdown.
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D3 (kanban drag-and-drop vs status dropdown).
- **Acceptance:** project create validates budget ≥ 0; lifecycle transitions follow the router state machine;
  task status changes persist from the chosen interaction; multi-assignee notifications fire to all assignees;
  ToDo CRUD scoped per task; audited.

## Epic 3 — Invoicing action surface (depends on F2)
- **Procedures:** `invoice.create/update`, `invoice.markSent/markPaid/void`, `invoice.recordPayment` (F2).
- **Entities:** `Invoice`, `InvoiceItem`, `InvoicePayment` (F2).
- **UI surface:** "New Invoice" = route (customer picker, due date, line-item editor with qty/unitPrice rows);
  edit = draft-only route. `invoices/[id]` (or row dropdown) gains markSent / markPaid / **record payment** /
  void actions. void = semi-destructive `AlertDialog` confirm.
- **Acceptance:** invoice create computes totals/tax; void blocked on already-paid per policy; recordPayment
  drives partial-payment status per F2; audited.

## Epic 4 — Money-movement (consistent confirm/authority UX)

### 4.1 Banking transactions (W6, 10 procedures)
- **Procedures:** `banking.create/update/toggleActive` (fund sources);
  `transaction.recordIncome/recordExpense/transfer/recordCreditCardCharge/payCreditCard/loanMoneyOutTo/
  loanMoneyIn/recordRefund/recordAdjustment`.
- **Entities:** `FundSource`, banking `Transaction`.
- **UI surface:** Add/Edit Fund Source = modal + a new `fund-sources/[id]` detail route (none exists today).
  Each money-movement type = a dedicated form (income, expense, transfer, CC charge, pay CC, loan out, loan in,
  refund, adjustment) — all money-affecting → `AlertDialog` confirm + authority gate + refetch.
- **Acceptance:** each transaction posts to the correct fund-source ledger; transfer validates distinct
  source/destination; adjustment requires reason; all audited.

### 4.2 POS session lifecycle + void (W3, 3 procedures)
- **Procedures:** `pos.session.open` (`{openingBalance, notes?}`), `pos.session.close`
  (`{id, closingBalance, notes?}`), `pos.sale.void` (`{id, reason}`).
- **Entities:** `POSSession`, `POSSale`, `POSSaleItem`, `StockMovement` (void writes offsetting `in` moves).
- **UI surface:** "Open Session" control on `pos/page.tsx` (router enforces one-open-session-per-user → surface
  the CONFLICT as a friendly error). "Close Session" on `pos/[id]/page.tsx` (router computes expected balance +
  discrepancy → show discrepancy review). Per-row "Void" on the sales table (reason required, semi-destructive
  → confirm + reason capture + refetch).
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D4 (Open Session modal vs dedicated route).
- **Acceptance:** opening blocks a second concurrent session; close surfaces computed discrepancy; void writes
  offsetting inventory and flips sale to `voided` in one transaction; all audited.

## Epic 5 — Service, Customer-facing, Platform, Notifications, Settings

### 5.1 Service — Job Orders + Support (W9, 8 procedures)
- **Procedures:** `jobOrder.create`, `jobOrder.assignTechnician`; `ticket.create/update/assign/changeStatus/
  close`, `comment.create`.
- **Entities:** `JobOrder`, `Ticket`, `TicketComment`, `TicketAttachment`.
- **UI surface:** "New Job Order" intake form (customer picker, device fields, reported issue, priority,
  estimated cost) + technician picker on detail. Support: "New Ticket" form, edit form, assignee picker (with
  user-name resolution — detail currently shows raw `User {id.slice(0,8)}`), status-action buttons driven by
  the ticket state machine (open → in_progress/waiting → resolved → closed), close action + resolution note,
  add-comment form with internal/public toggle.
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D5 (duplicate job-order detail routes — consolidation).
- **Acceptance:** job-order intake creates with status `pending`; ticket status changes obey the router state
  machine; assignee resolves to a display name; comments respect internal/public visibility; audited.

### 5.2 Storefront — authenticated checkout + order history (W10, 2 procedures)
- **Procedures:** `storefront.listMyOrders`, `storefront.placeOrder` (authenticated `writeProcedure`, distinct
  from the existing public `placeOrderAsCustomer`).
- **Entities:** `EcommerceOrder`, `EcommerceOrderItem`, `Customer`.
- **UI surface:** customer-facing "My Orders" history page (authenticated account area). `placeOrder` =
  staff/admin "create order on behalf of customer" form (customer picker + line-item builder) **and/or** an
  authenticated-customer checkout path.
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D6 (how authenticated storefront customers are modeled + whether
  `placeOrder` is a staff-on-behalf tool, a logged-in-customer checkout, or both).
- **Acceptance:** My Orders lists only the authenticated customer's orders (tenant + customer scoped);
  placeOrder deducts stock on payment confirmation per existing order rules; audited.

### 5.3 Notifications surface (W11)
- **Build:** replace the `notificationRouter` **stub** (`list`/`unreadCount`/`markRead`/`markAllRead` return
  empty/0) with a real backend, and wire the dead header bell.
- **Entities:** new persistent `Notification` model (id, userId, type, payload, readAt, createdAt) + Valkey
  for unread-count fan-out / real-time.
- **Procedures:** the four existing stubs, now backed.
- **UI surface:** header-bell popover/inbox (list, mark-read, mark-all-read, badge, empty state).
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D7 (Valkey-backed ephemeral vs Prisma `Notification` durable store).
- **Acceptance:** a domain event creates a notification; unread count reflects in the badge; mark-read clears
  it; popover renders empty state when none.

### 5.4 Settings sub-pages (W11, 5 surfaces)
- **Build:** `settings/users`, `settings/departments`, `settings/expense-categories`, `settings/smtp`,
  `settings/account` (only `settings/xendit` exists today).
- **Entities:** `User`/role assignments, `Department`, `ExpenseCategory`, tenant SMTP config, tenant
  plan/billing.
- **UI surface:** per-page CRUD/config: user+role management, department tree, expense-category editor
  (seeded defaults deactivate-only per schema), SMTP config form, account/plan/billing view.
- **Acceptance:** each page performs its CRUD against tenant-scoped data; default expense categories cannot be
  deleted (only deactivated); role changes gated to tenant authority; audited.

### 5.5 Platform-admin hardening (W12, depends on F1)
- **Build:** route the existing `powerbyte-admin` RSC pages/Server Actions through `platformRouter`
  (`listTenants/getTenant/suspendTenant/reactivateTenant`) via the F1 server-caller, to gain
  `platformProcedure` auth + L5 audit logging (`PLATFORM:SUSPEND_TENANT` / `PLATFORM:REACTIVATE_TENANT`).
  Surface `listTenants` search/status/pagination on the admin list page.
- **Entities:** `Tenant`, `TenantAuditLog` (public schema).
- **UI surface:** reason-capture on suspend/reactivate (router requires `reason: min(1)`); search box + status
  filter + pagination on the tenant list.
- **⚠ NEEDS OWNER DECISION:** see Decision D8 (suspension reason-capture UX — modal textarea vs inline).
- **Acceptance:** suspend/reactivate write `PLATFORM:*` AuditLog rows; list honors search/status/pagination;
  platform-owner-only access enforced at the data layer.

## ⚠ Owner Decisions (consolidated)

- **D1 — Invoice payment ↔ Banking auto-post.** When `invoice.recordPayment` runs, auto-create a Banking
  income transaction against the chosen fund source, or keep it a separate manual entry?
  *Options:* (a) auto-post (one action, fewer steps, tighter ledger coupling); (b) manual (explicit control,
  matches current discrete-action pattern). **Recommended default: (a) auto-post** — Orqafy's thesis is
  "every peso traces to a fund source," so coupling payment to the ledger is on-brand.

- **D2 — DTR time-clock device model.** `attendanceClockIn/Out` UX: per-user widget in the web app, a shared
  kiosk mode, or mobile-only (Expo)?
  *Options:* (a) per-user web widget; (b) shared kiosk terminal; (c) mobile clock with GPS.
  **Recommended default: (a) per-user web widget now, (c) mobile later** — fastest to ship; GPS clock fits the
  field-staff roadmap but is a larger build.

- **D3 — Kanban interaction.** `tasks.taskUpdateStatus` via drag-and-drop or a per-card status dropdown?
  *Options:* (a) drag-and-drop (richer, more client code/edge cases); (b) status dropdown (simpler, accessible).
  **Recommended default: (b) dropdown for v1, (a) as a follow-up** — ships the capability without the DnD risk.

- **D4 — POS Open Session UX.** Modal on `pos/page.tsx` or a dedicated `pos/sessions/new` route?
  *Options:* (a) modal (in-context, fast); (b) route (deep-linkable).
  **Recommended default: (a) modal** — opening a session is a 2-field in-context action.

- **D5 — Duplicate job-order detail routes.** `job-orders/[id]` (read-only ops) and `service/job-orders/[id]`
  (interactive technician) coexist; the list links to the read-only one and nothing links to the interactive one.
  *Options:* (a) make the interactive view canonical, redirect/retire the read-only one, add a
  `service/job-orders` list; (b) keep both with distinct roles.
  **Recommended default: (a) consolidate on the interactive view** before building `jobOrder.create` intake.

- **D6 — Authenticated storefront customer model + `placeOrder` role.** How are logged-in storefront customers
  modeled, and is `placeOrder` a staff "order on behalf" tool, a logged-in-customer checkout, or both?
  *Options:* (a) staff-on-behalf only; (b) logged-in-customer checkout only; (c) both.
  **Recommended default: (c) both, staff-on-behalf first** — reuses the line-item builder and unblocks the more
  common internal flow sooner.

- **D7 — Notification store.** Valkey-backed ephemeral notifications or a durable Prisma `Notification` model
  (with Valkey only for real-time fan-out)?
  *Options:* (a) Valkey-only ephemeral; (b) Prisma durable + Valkey fan-out.
  **Recommended default: (b) Prisma durable + Valkey fan-out** — survives restarts, queryable history, matches
  the schema-as-source-of-truth posture.

- **D8 — Platform suspend/reactivate reason-capture UX.** `reason: min(1)` is required by the router.
  *Options:* (a) `AlertDialog` with a required textarea; (b) inline expandable row field.
  **Recommended default: (a) AlertDialog + textarea** — consistent with every other authority action in the app.

## Deliberately scoped OUT (not Phase-7 features)

- **Already-fully-wired / redundant-but-covered surfaces** logged in the waves (CRM interactive quotation +
  contact-log surface, the POS terminal `cart-client.tsx`, the e-commerce storefront list/detail/checkout/guest
  tracking, `storefront.browseProducts` / `storefront.listAllOrders`, all working nav/filter/pagination
  controls). These are not gaps — no action.
- **Wiring-program nav/dead-control fixes already shipped** on `swarm/wire-dead-controls` (e.g. customer row
  links, clients list wire, store "Track order" link, reports tenant-isolation fix, settings dead-link cleanup).
  Done, not respecced here.
- **Testimonials CMS / admin UI** — PRODUCT.md marks it out of scope for v1 (hardcoded seed). Excluded.
- **"Calendar view" for Tasks** — PRODUCT.md/placeholder labels it a later phase; excluded from this backend
  wave (it is a view-layer build, no unsurfaced mutation).
- **Vendor detail page as a pure nav fix** — building `vendors/[id]` is folded into the Purchasing epic
  (2.1) as part of the vendor CRUD surface, not treated as a standalone nav item.
